bends.note: 3rd rises ENE west of Eggleston (south face of the sheet-125 block at y~557, pipes y~440/505 at x 1250) and runs almost due E east of it (south face y~443)

notes: Streets: E. 3RD (top edge, 50' printed; north face off the scan east of Eggleston, so centre taken 25 ft north of the south frontage line y~443-446, which matches the midline of its two pipes), EGGLESTON AV. (91', railroad tracks curving through it; west face is the outline of the sheet-125 block, x~1423 at 3rd and ~1793 at Pearl; east face the block line labelled EGGLESTON, x~1760 at 3rd and ~2100 at Pearl), ELLEN (18' printed at y~830; faces about x~2860/2935), KILGOUR (east edge; printed KILGOUR and 40'; west face x~3770-3775, east face off the scan, pipe at x~3828; centre taken west face plus 20 ft, which falls on the scan edge at x~3840), E. PEARL (60', north faces y~1700-1715, south face y~1905-1920), E. FRONT (60', runs ENE across the rail yard from the bridge approach to the east edge with no crossings on this sheet; its west end abuts the bridge approach strip at x~395 beside the stone pier and the ticket office, where sheet 106 records Butler/Front). Ellen meets 3rd only through a very narrow (about 7 ft) gap between lots 829 and 831 (x~2895-2918); the 18 ft street opens out from y~790 southward. It is recorded as a T at 3rd on this sheet (sheet 126 continues Ellen north of 3rd). South of the ELLEN label the same 18 ft strip (x~2885-2935) is printed (PRIVATE COURT) down to Pearl, with 18' printed at its mouth; it is recorded as Ellen/Pearl T with that caveat (drop it if private courts are not wanted). Eggleston and Kilgour both end at Pearl (train sheds and tracks south of it). BUTLER: the label is printed at the west edge, inside the strip x~245-395 that also carries the APPROACH TO BRIDGE label; Butler's own pipe runs along the scan edge at x~125, so its centreline is at or past the edge and Butler/Pearl and Butler/Front are left to sheet 106 (which recorded them). The approach strip is not recorded as a street, matching sheet 106. Railroad tracks, train sheds and freight houses ignored.
